question: Which set of organs belongs to the internal structures of the male reproductive system?

options.A: Prepuce and glans penis
options.B: Scrotal skin and dartos muscle
options.C: Testes and accessory glands
options.D: Scrotum and penile shaft

explanation: Internal structures include the testes, duct system, and accessory glands, while the scrotum and penis are external. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T2#GNS216_U2_T2_h1)

question: A patient tells you they stopped taking their daily allopurinol because their toe stopped hurting. What is your best nursing advice?

options.A: Suggest they double the dose of allopurinol whenever they eat red meat or drink alcohol
options.B: Confirm that they no longer need any medication since the pain has completely gone away
options.C: Explain that the medication must be taken daily to keep uric acid low and prevent future attacks
options.D: Advise them to switch to taking ibuprofen every time they feel a slight twinge in the toe

explanation: You've got it! Allopurinol isn't a painkiller for a single attack—it's a daily maintenance routine. Stopping it lets uric acid climb right back up and brings the pain back. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T16#GNS222_U1_T16_h7)

question: Who are considered key stakeholders in community mobilisation?

options.A: Traditional rulers and religious leaders
options.B: Pharmaceutical company owners only
options.C: Patients admitted to distant urban hospitals
options.D: Only foreign aid workers from abroad

explanation: Traditional and religious leaders are influential figures who help guide community opinions and behaviours. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T2#GNS124_U4_T2_h4)

question: What is the term for weak, lazy uterine contractions that fail to open the cervix?

options.A: Occiput posterior
options.B: Cephalopelvic disproportion
options.C: Uterine inertia
options.D: Uterine hyperstimulation

explanation: Spot on! 'Inertia' means lack of movement or energy. The uterus is simply too tired or weak to push the process along. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T003#GNS226_U3_T003_h4)

question: What is the main thing that separates a true experiment from a quasi-experiment?

options.A: Avoiding all forms of statistical testing
options.B: The use of patient interviews for data collection
options.C: The presence of a clinical nurse researcher
options.D: Random assignment of participants to groups

explanation: You nailed it! True experiments use random chance (like flipping a coin) to drop people into different groups, while quasi-experiments don't use strict random mixing. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T13#GNS217_U3_T13_h4)

question: What often causes health policies to fail during implementation?

options.A: Medical doctors writing too many discharge summaries
options.B: Too many nurses participating in hospital board meetings
options.C: Patients refusing to take free prescribed medications
options.D: Poor funding, corruption, and lack of political will

explanation: Even great laws on paper fail if leaders do not provide money or commitment to execute them properly. [learn more](GST321_U6_T3#GST321_U6_T3_h7)

question: What advice should a nurse give a patient taking oral prednisone to protect their stomach?

options.A: Take the medication on an empty stomach.
options.B: Crush the pills and dissolve them in juice.
options.C: Take the medication right before going to bed.
options.D: Take the medication with food or milk.

explanation: Correct! Steroids can be harsh on the gut lining, so taking them with food, milk, or a meal helps prevent stomach upset. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T3#GNS223_U5_T3_h9)

question: Where are brush border enzymes like lactase and maltase found?

options.A: Embedded in the membrane of small intestine cells
options.B: Floating freely inside the cavity of the stomach
options.C: Released by the gallbladder during fat digestion
options.D: Produced by the salivary glands in the mouth

explanation: These enzymes live right on the microvilli of the small intestine lining, ready to finish breaking down your sugars. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T11#GNS121_U1_T11_h6)

question: How does the myelin coating affect the speed of an electrical signal traveling down a nerve fiber?

options.A: It increases impulse speed via saltatory conduction
options.B: It has no effect on nerve conduction velocity
options.C: It stops the impulse entirely until it reaches a synapse
options.D: It slows impulse speed by creating resistance

explanation: Myelin acts like insulation on an electrical wire. It lets the signal jump rapidly from one node to the next, speeding things up tremendously! [learn more](GNS211_U3_T6#GNS211_U3_T6_h5)

question: What is a common pitfall parents fall into when a toddler's appetite drops?

options.A: Stopping all forms of milk consumption immediately
options.B: Giving the child adult-sized portions at every meal
options.C: Providing too many green leafy vegetables
options.D: Forcing food or offering constant sugary snacks

explanation: When toddlers eat less, worried parents sometimes force meals or hand over sugary snacks, which unfortunately leads to picky eating habits. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T012#GNS227_U7_T012_h4)

question: According to the Spaulding classification, how must you process a medical tool that goes deep inside sterile body tissues?

options.A: Simple soap washing
options.B: Sterilization
options.C: High-level disinfection
options.D: Low-level disinfection

explanation: If a tool enters sterile body tissues or blood vessels, it's a critical item and absolutely must be fully sterilized! [learn more](GST114_U2_T10#GST114_U2_T10_h6)

question: What is the simple difference between isolation and quarantine?

options.A: Isolation is used only for animals, while quarantine is used exclusively for human beings.
options.B: Isolation requires medication, while quarantine involves only dietary changes.
options.C: Isolation is voluntary, while quarantine is always legally enforced by police.
options.D: Isolation separates sick people with a disease, while quarantine separates people exposed to a disease who might become sick.

explanation: Remember: Isolation is for those who are *already sick*, while quarantine is for those who were *exposed* and are waiting to see if they'll fall ill. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T87#GNS214_U1_T87_h6)

question: If a patient has an infection causing nausea, vomiting, and watery stool, what is the most important thing to watch out for?

options.A: Sudden muscle hypertrophy
options.B: Elevated blood pressure
options.C: Fluid volume deficit
options.D: High red blood cell count

explanation: Exactly right! Vomiting and diarrhea drain body fluids fast, putting the patient at high risk for dehydration. [learn more](GST114_U2_T4#GST114_U2_T4_h5)

question: Which macronutrient packs the most calories into every single gram?

options.A: Fat
options.B: Protein
options.C: Water
options.D: Carbohydrate

explanation: Fat gives us 9 calories per gram, while carbs and protein only give 4. That makes fat our most energy-dense nutrient! [learn more](GNS227_U4_T007#GNS227_U4_T007_h3)

question: During non-surgical care for a kidney injury, which nursing sign is most important to report immediately?

options.A: An increase in sleepiness after receiving a scheduled pain medication
options.B: Mild bruising fading to a yellow color around the flank area
options.C: A sudden drop in blood pressure paired with a fast heart rate
options.D: A slight yellow tinge in the normal daily urine output

explanation: A fast heart rate and dropping blood pressure are early warning signs of hidden internal bleeding. Catching this early can save a life! [learn more](GNS213_U4_T10#GNS213_U4_T10_h6)

question: Which breathing sound tells you right away that a patient has an upper airway obstruction?

options.A: Crackles
options.B: Wheezing
options.C: Friction rub
options.D: Stridor

explanation: Stridor is that high-pitched, strained sound you hear when air is struggling to push past a blockage in the upper airway. You can often hear it without a stethoscope! [learn more](GNS213_U2_T4#GNS213_U2_T4_h4)

question: Which body part is mainly affected in Type I FGM?

options.A: The outer labia majora only
options.B: The Bartholin glands
options.C: The clitoris and its prepuce
options.D: The entire vaginal wall

explanation: Spot on! Type I involves removing part or all of the clitoris and its surrounding skin fold (the prepuce). You're learning fast! [learn more](GNS225_U6_T2#GNS225_U6_T2_h3)

question: What is the standard first-line treatment given to pregnant women with iron deficiency anaemia?

options.A: High-dose intravenous antibiotics
options.B: Routine whole blood transfusions
options.C: Oral iron supplements
options.D: Intramuscular vitamin B12 injections

explanation: Simple and effective! Oral iron tablets are the go-to first step in antenatal clinics to help build back the mother's iron stores safely. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T020#GNS226_U2_T020_h7)

question: What does an odds ratio of greater than 1 tell us?

options.A: The exposure is a risk factor for the disease
options.B: There is no association between exposure and disease
options.C: The exposure protects against the disease
options.D: The study results are completely invalid

explanation: Brilliant! An odds ratio above 1 means the exposure showed up more often in the sick group, pointing to it as a potential risk factor. [learn more](GST114_U2_T19#GST114_U2_T19_h4)

question: A community midwife visits a mother four days after delivery at home. What should be the primary focus of this visit?

options.A: Starting the baby on solid foods to boost early growth
options.B: Administering a complete set of adolescent reproductive counseling
options.C: Scheduling the mother for immediate return to work duties
options.D: Checking breastfeeding attachment, uterine involution, and lochia

explanation: Early postnatal visits prioritize assessing physical recovery, checking the uterus and lochia, and ensuring proper breastfeeding to prevent early complications. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T14#GNS225_U3_T14_h3)

question: A patient regains a pulse after cardiac arrest but remains unconscious. What is a key focus of their nursing care now?

options.A: Discharging the patient home with a portable oxygen tank
options.B: Weaning off all cardiac monitoring equipment within one hour
options.C: Encouraging immediate oral intake of food and fluids
options.D: Protecting neurological function through targeted temperature management

explanation: Controlled cooling helps protect the brain from injury after it went without oxygen during the arrest. You're safeguarding their recovery! [learn more](GNS321_U2_T7#GNS321_U2_T7_h6)

question: A patient says their knee pain gets worse when climbing stairs and feels better when resting. Which part of PQRST is this?

options.A: Pain severity and scale
options.B: Timing and frequency
options.C: Provoking and palliating factors
options.D: Region and radiation

explanation: Well done! Things that trigger pain (like stairs) are provoking factors, and things that soothe it (like rest) are palliating factors. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T2#GNS222_U1_T2_h4)

question: Which nursing action helps build instant trust with a newly admitted PAC patient?

options.A: Reviewing the client's chart at the nursing station before entering
options.B: Asking the client to sign financial clearance forms immediately
options.C: Instructing visitors to leave the ward before nursing assessment begins
options.D: Explaining every clinical procedure clearly before touching the client

explanation: Telling her what you are about to do shows deep respect for her body and eases the fear of feeling helpless in the hospital. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T025#GNS226_U5_T025_h5)

question: What is the main goal of an electrophysiologic study (EPS)?

options.A: To clear blocked plaque from the coronary arteries
options.B: To measure the exact volume of blood pumped per minute
options.C: To record surface electrical signals without touching the heart
options.D: To map the electrical system of the heart from the inside

explanation: Think of an EPS as an electrical wiring check! Special tiny wires (catheters) are put right inside the heart chambers to see how the electrical signals are flowing. You've got this! [learn more](GNS222_U3_T10#GNS222_U3_T10_h1)

question: What does medication adherence mean in daily nursing practice?

options.A: How closely a patient follows their prescribed treatment plan
options.B: The ability of a doctor to write clear prescriptions
options.C: The speed at which a drug is absorbed into the bloodstream
options.D: How strictly a pharmacy records daily drug sales

explanation: Adherence measures whether a patient takes their medications correctly regarding timing, dosage, and frequency as agreed upon with their healthcare provider. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T2#GNS215_U4_T2_h1)

question: Why might people from different ethnic or genetic backgrounds process the same medication at different speeds?

options.A: The amount of water they drink hourly
options.B: How many meals they eat each day
options.C: Genetic variations in drug metabolism
options.D: The specific brand of pharmacy they use

explanation: Our genes naturally influence how liver enzymes break down drugs, meaning different people can process medications at different rates. Great to keep in mind for safe care! [learn more](GNS125_U3_T3#GNS125_U3_T3_h4)

question: Which of these conditions is a classic reason to use a Nelson inhaler?

options.A: Acute sinusitis
options.B: Bacterial pneumonia
options.C: Spontaneous pneumothorax
options.D: Pulmonary edema

explanation: Spot on! Sinusitis brings painful inflammation and blocked nasal passages, which respond wonderfully to the warm, soothing moisture of steam therapy. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T6#GNS212_U2_T6_h3)

question: What is a top priority for nursing care right after a laparoscopy?

options.A: Monitoring vital signs and checking for signs of bleeding or pain
options.B: Performing a complete neurological examination of the lower limbs
options.C: Removing surgical stitches before the doctor arrives on the ward
options.D: Discharging the patient home without waiting for full recovery

explanation: Spot on! Right after surgery, keeping an eye on vital signs and watching for bleeding or heavy pain keeps our patient safe. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T5#GNS311_U1_T5_h7)

question: What is the immediate impact of early marriage on a young girl's education?

options.A: Immediate promotion to higher academic grades
options.B: An abrupt end to her formal education
options.C: Free government-funded university placement
options.D: Mandatory transfer to an adult night school

explanation: Spot on! Heavy household chores and early pregnancies almost always force young brides to drop out of school for good. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T11#GNS312_U1_T11_h5)

question: What score shows a normal, healthy deep tendon reflex?
explanation: A score of 2+ is the standard, expected normal response for deep tendon reflexes in healthy adults. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T2#GNS222_U3_T2_h7)

question: Why do nurses convert raw tally numbers into percentages and rates when analyzing data?

options.A: To make the final report look more complicated to read
options.B: To eliminate the need to collect any information from households
options.C: To make the health findings easier to interpret and compare
options.D: To prevent community members from understanding the results

explanation: Spot on! Percentages and rates give meaning to raw numbers, helping us clearly see the proportion of people affected by an issue. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T18#GNS225_U2_T18_h6)

question: Why is getting enough calcium so crucial for a breastfeeding mother?

options.A: To prevent the baby from developing infantile jaundice
options.B: To make the breast milk taste sweet to the infant
options.C: To ensure the infant's skin develops normally
options.D: To prevent the depletion of her own bone density

explanation: Calcium constantly flows into breast milk. If a mum's diet is low in calcium, her body will borrow it right out of her own bones to protect the milk. Protect those bones, mummies! [learn more](GNS227_U2_T013#GNS227_U2_T013_h4)

question: What is the golden rule of fluid balance when it comes to sodium?

options.A: Sodium ignores fluid shifts
options.B: Water follows sodium
options.C: Sodium follows protein
options.D: Water pushes sodium out

explanation: You got it! Think of sodium as a magnet—wherever sodium goes, water is definitely going to follow it. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T008#GNS227_U6_T008_h2)

question: Which service is especially helpful for giving family caregivers of individuals with ASD a much-needed break?

options.A: Respite care services
options.B: Sudden medication changes
options.C: Mandatory legal arbitration
options.D: Extended hospital admission

explanation: Spot on! Caring for someone full-time is heavy work. Respite care gives families a temporary break to rest and recharge. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T5#GNS324_U4_T5_h6)

question: What is the main job of mifepristone during a medical abortion?

options.A: Stimulating strong uterine contractions
options.B: Inducing systemic maternal hypertension
options.C: Blocking progesterone receptors to detach the sac
options.D: Paralyzing the musculature of the cervix

explanation: You've got this! Mifepristone blocks progesterone, the hormone needed to maintain pregnancy. This causes the uterine lining to soften and detaches the sac, preparing the way for the next step. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T011#GNS226_U5_T011_h1)

question: A healthy adult client closes their eyes and relaxes quietly. Which brain wave pattern is most likely to become dominant?

options.A: Beta waves
options.B: Theta waves
options.C: Delta waves
options.D: Alpha waves

explanation: When you close your eyes and just chill out, your brain shifts into alpha wave mode. You've got this! [learn more](GNS222_U3_T9#GNS222_U3_T9_h1)

question: Why is drying a newborn immediately after birth so crucial?

options.A: It washes away skin oils
options.B: It lowers their heart rate to normal
options.C: It stimulates breathing and keeps them warm
options.D: It stops baby jaundice from developing

explanation: Drying wipes away wet fluid so the baby doesn't get chilled from evaporation, and the rubbing action acts as a gentle nudge telling them to breathe! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T011#GNS226_U1_T011_h3)

question: What can happen if you mix certain suspensions with the wrong type of liquid?

options.A: The liquid immediately changes into a bright gas
options.B: The drug becomes twice as potent instantly
options.C: The active drug may precipitate or break down
options.D: The medication turns into a solid plastic block

explanation: Chemical reactions can ruin a drug! Mixing incompatible fluids can cause the medicine to clump up, fall apart, or lose its healing power. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T21#GNS122_U1_T21_h5)

question: A patient says they feel constantly exhausted, lack energy for simple chores, and sleep does not help at all. How should you, as the nurse, categorize this?

options.A: As normal tiredness
options.B: As circadian misalignment
options.C: As acute somnolence
options.D: As clinical fatigue

explanation: Well done! When sleep doesn't touch the exhaustion and it starts disrupting daily life, we call it clinical fatigue rather than regular tiredness. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T3#GNS123_U3_T3_h2)

question: Which vitamin is most commonly recommended as a first-line supplement for pregnancy nausea?

options.A: Vitamin D
options.B: Vitamin A
options.C: Vitamin C
options.D: Vitamin B6

explanation: Pyridoxine (Vitamin B6) is a safe, go-to supplement prescribed in antenatal clinics to help ease that queasy feeling. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T011#GNS226_U2_T011_h5)

question: Why do community health nurses conduct home visits for high-risk families?

options.A: To enforce strict fines on parents who fail to pay their taxes
options.B: To remove all children permanently from homes experiencing poverty
options.C: To monitor child development and assess safety hazards in the living environment
options.D: To conduct major surgical procedures without hospital equipment

explanation: Correct! Home visits help nurses see how children are living, check for safety issues, and offer supportive guidance to the family. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T4#GNS225_U5_T4_h5)

question: A patient just took a morning injection of regular (short-acting) insulin. When should the nurse watch out for the highest risk of low blood sugar?

options.A: Twelve to twenty-four hours after injection
options.B: Two to three hours after injection
options.C: Ten minutes after injection
options.D: Immediately upon skin puncture

explanation: You got it! Short-acting insulin usually peaks around 2 to 3 hours, meaning that's when blood sugar drops the fastest and needs close monitoring. [learn more](GNS223_U7_T1#GNS223_U7_T1_h3)

question: How does metabolic stress differ from simple starvation?

options.A: Metabolic stress lowers the heart rate to save body nutrients.
options.B: Metabolic stress forces high energy use while blocking normal tissue conservation.
options.C: Simple starvation causes sudden swelling all over the body.
options.D: Simple starvation causes a faster breakdown of muscle than major trauma.

explanation: While simple starvation triggers energy-saving mechanisms, inflammatory metabolic stress forces continuous tissue breakdown without letting the body conserve resources. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T023#GNS227_U2_T023_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of an action plan during a project?

options.A: To raise funds from international organizations after the event
options.B: To change the objectives after the project has already started
options.C: To outline who is responsible for each task, the timeline, and required resources
options.D: To grade community members based on their health test scores

explanation: An action plan keeps everyone organized. It clearly shows who is doing what, when they are doing it, and what tools they need. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T7#GNS124_U5_T7_h6)

question: How is droplet transmission different from airborne transmission?

options.A: Airborne pathogens cannot infect human respiratory tracts
options.B: Droplets only transmit fungal infections, while airborne transmits bacteria
options.C: Droplets are heavier, fall quickly within a short distance, and do not linger in the air
options.D: Droplet transmission requires direct skin-to-skin contact between patients

explanation: Think of droplets (from a cough or sneeze) as heavy rocks that quickly drop to the ground within a meter, while airborne germs are like dust that floats around. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T82#GNS214_U1_T82_h5)

question: Which factor makes a woman more likely to get vulval varicosities in her later pregnancies?

options.A: Early menarche
options.B: High dietary iron
options.C: Multiparity
options.D: First pregnancy

explanation: Multiparity just means having had multiple pregnancies! Each time, the pelvic veins stretch out a bit more, making them more prone to swelling in future pregnancies. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T9#GNS216_U5_T9_h3)

question: Besides nerve signals, what else can trigger smooth muscle to contract?

options.A: Somatic nerve stimulation via the spinal cord
options.B: Direct voluntary relaxation exercises
options.C: Circulating hormones and local chemical changes
options.D: Conscious thoughts from the cerebral cortex

explanation: Smooth muscle is super responsive! It reacts to hormones in the blood, stretching, and local chemical shifts like oxygen or acid levels to keep your body balanced. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T11#GNS121_U3_T11_h5)

question: What role does the community health nurse play during participatory community diagnosis?

options.A: A politician who promises free money for everyone
options.B: A facilitator who guides and works alongside the community
options.C: A distant observer who never talks to local residents
options.D: A strict commander who gives orders without explanation

explanation: Nurses work collaboratively with local people to empower them rather than imposing solutions from above. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T3#GNS124_U3_T3_h4)

question: Oh no! A scrub nurse receives a broken suture needle from the surgeon. What should they do first?

options.A: Ask the surgeon to replace the needle holder
options.B: Wait until the end of the operation to mention the break
options.C: Ensure all pieces of the broken needle are accounted for
options.D: Throw the broken pieces into the general waste bin

explanation: You are learning fast! Every single piece of a broken sharp must be found right away so nothing is left inside the patient. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T8#GNS123_U5_T8_h2)

question: Why must a nurse instruct a patient to remove all metal jewelry and hairpins before a musculoskeletal CT scan?

options.A: The scanner's suction will pull metal objects into the machine.
options.B: Metal interacts with the magnetic field to cause severe burns.
options.C: Metal objects cause artifacts that ruin the clarity of the images.
options.D: Metal pieces block the patient from breathing properly.

explanation: Dense metal creates bright streaks and shadowing on CT scans, known as artifacts, which can hide important details about bones and joints. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T6#GNS222_U1_T6_h3)

question: How does tuberculosis mostly spread from one person to another?

options.A: Ingestion of unpasteurized dairy products
options.B: Direct contact with contaminated skin lesions
options.C: Inhalation of airborne droplet nuclei
options.D: Sharing eating utensils and drinking cups

explanation: When someone with active TB coughs or sneezes, tiny droplets float into the air. If others breathe them in, they can catch the infection too. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T18#GNS324_U4_T18_h1)

question: Why is newborn screening so important for babies with sickle cell anaemia?

options.A: It prevents the spleen from ever being damaged by blocked blood vessels
options.B: It stops red blood cells from ever changing into a crescent shape
options.C: It allows early penicillin prophylaxis and vaccination before severe infections occur
options.D: It cures the genetic mutation completely before symptoms start to show

explanation: Early detection saves lives! Finding the condition early lets doctors start daily penicillin and special vaccines right away, protecting the baby from dangerous infections. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T7#GNS311_U2_T7_h3)

question: When we talk about resource mobilization for a project, what does it include besides money?

options.A: Gathering medical supplies, outreach spaces, and local volunteers
options.B: Closing down existing health posts to save money
options.C: Reducing the number of staff required to run the clinic
options.D: Waiting for international organizations to supply all equipment

explanation: Resources aren't just cash in hand. They include everything from a good venue for outreach to willing volunteers and basic supplies. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T20#GNS225_U2_T20_h3)

question: A ward tries a new handwashing protocol. After one month, how do they check if it's working?

options.A: Assume it's working because nobody complained at the meeting
options.B: Compare current audit data against the baseline measurements taken before starting
options.C: Wait five years before checking infection stats
options.D: Ask the head nurse if the ward looks cleaner

explanation: Brilliant! You always compare your current results to your original baseline. Numbers don't lie, and it's the only way to prove real progress. [learn more](GST319_U1_T4#GST319_U1_T4_h7)

question: How do screen-readers and talking appliances primarily help a visually impaired patient?

options.A: By physically guiding the patient's hands across household objects
options.B: By curing the underlying disease causing progressive blindness
options.C: By translating digital text and operational cues into audio feedback
options.D: By directly improving the optical clarity of damaged retinal tissues

explanation: Technology is amazing! When eyes need a break or can't see, turning text and appliance settings into spoken audio lets patients stay independent and in control. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T8#GNS311_U3_T8_h3)

question: Within how many days of life is ophthalmia neonatorum typically diagnosed in a newborn?

options.A: Within the first twenty-eight days of life
options.B: Only during the first forty-eight hours
options.C: After six weeks of postnatal development
options.D: Between two and three months of age

explanation: You've got this! Ophthalmia neonatorum is simply eye inflammation that shows up during the first 28 days of a baby's life. Keep up the great studying! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T019#GNS226_U3_T019_h1)

question: What is the primary focus of palliative care for terminal patients at home?

options.A: Finding a surgical cure for advanced cancer
options.B: Testing new experimental drugs that reverse aging
options.C: Isolating the patient from all family and friends
options.D: Providing comfort, symptom control, and preserving dignity

explanation: Palliative care centers on relieving pain and managing symptoms to ensure the highest possible quality of life. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T8#GNS324_U1_T8_h5)

question: Why is checking for malnutrition important before a patient goes for surgery?

options.A: It shortens the time the patient spends in the recovery room
options.B: It completely eliminates the need for any intravenous fluids
options.C: It ensures the patient will never feel nauseated after waking up
options.D: It helps the body withstand surgical stress and prevents complications

explanation: Spot on! Well-nourished patients handle the stress of an operation much better and have a lower risk of infections. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T009#GNS227_U7_T009_h1)

question: A pregnant mum asks why she needs to eat protein foods like beans and fish. What is the best way to explain this?

options.A: They provide extra sugar to keep your energy levels very high
options.B: They supply protein which helps build the placenta and baby's tissues
options.C: They prevent morning sickness by soothing your stomach lining
options.D: They replace the need for taking any blood-building vitamins

explanation: Protein is like the building blocks for construction! It helps build the baby's muscles, organs, and the placenta too. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T012#GNS227_U2_T012_h2)

question: Which of these nursing duties counts as a skilled nursing intervention?

options.A: Managing complex wound care and dressing changes.
options.B: Assisting a resident with walking down the hallway.
options.C: Handing out meal trays to all residents at lunchtime.
options.D: Helping a resident put on their casual daytime clothes.

question: Which of these is NOT a common barrier to good teamwork?

question: Why is it important to involve local leaders right from the start of a health project?

question: How should a nurse view providing reproductive health education to teenagers?

question: Which instrument is most commonly used for safe uterine evacuation during PAC procedures?

question: How is a nursing diagnosis different from a medical diagnosis?

options.A: A medical diagnosis describes how a patient feels emotionally
options.B: A nursing diagnosis focuses on how the patient responds to health conditions
options.C: A medical diagnosis can only be made by a registered nurse
options.D: A nursing diagnosis identifies the exact pathology of a disease

explanation: You've got this! A medical diagnosis names the disease itself (like malaria), while a nursing diagnosis focuses on how the patient reacts to it (like feeling exhausted or in pain). [learn more](GNS123_U4_T7#GNS123_U4_T7_h3)

question: What personal quality is essential for a nurse caring for patients with substance use disorders?

options.A: Willingness to lecture and scold patients about their past mistakes
options.B: Strict refusal to administer any form of pain relief medication
options.C: Belief that addiction is simply a moral failing and personal choice
options.D: Self-awareness to recognize and manage personal biases against addiction

explanation: To give truly professional care, we must check our personal judgments at the door and treat every patient with empathy. [learn more](GNS125_U4_T3#GNS125_U4_T3_h8)

question: What is the usual time gap between taking mifepristone and misoprostol?

options.A: Exactly one week apart
options.B: 24 to 48 hours
options.C: Immediately at the same time
options.D: 12 to 14 days apart

explanation: You'll often see 24 to 48 hours prescribed—this gives the first drug enough time to do its job so the second drug can work effectively. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T012#GNS226_U5_T012_h4)

question: A patient is prescribed a sustained-release capsule for chronic pain. What must the nurse tell the patient about taking this medication?

options.A: Swallow the capsule whole without chewing or crushing
options.B: Chew the capsule thoroughly before swallowing with water
options.C: Crush the capsule into food if swallowing is difficult
options.D: Open the shell and dissolve the powder in hot water

explanation: Crushing or chewing sustained-release medications destroys their special mechanism and causes a dangerous, immediate release of the entire drug dose. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T7#GNS125_U2_T7_h2)

question: A newly intubated patient is on a ventilator. You notice the left side of the chest is barely moving and you cannot hear breath sounds there. What likely happened?

options.A: The ventilator settings have too much positive end-expiratory pressure
options.B: The tube has slipped into the right mainstem bronchus
options.C: The oxygen source has become disconnected from the machine
options.D: The patient is developing a severe tension pneumothorax

explanation: The right breathing pipe (bronchus) is a straight shot down, so tubes often slide too far in and end up ventilating only the right lung, leaving the left side quiet. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T10#GNS321_U2_T10_h3)

question: What is an essential nursing duty when caring for a patient with acute poisoning?

options.A: Leaving the patient alone to rest quietly in a dark room
options.B: Gathering the history, securing samples, and keeping the bedside safe
options.C: Disposing of all empty medication containers immediately
options.D: Prescribing the final discharge medications without doctor review

explanation: Nurses act as detectives! Collecting pill bottles, noting what was taken, and keeping the patient safe from harm are key parts of emergency care. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T7#GNS215_U5_T7_h7)

question: A test report shows extremely high acid output and multiple stomach ulcers. Which condition does this suggest?

options.A: Zollinger-Ellison syndrome
options.B: Chronic atrophic gastritis
options.C: Pyloric valve stenosis
options.D: Pernicious anemia

explanation: Zollinger-Ellison syndrome involves tumors that produce gastrin, driving massive, unrelenting acid production that creates severe ulcers. You're building solid pathology knowledge! [learn more](GNS213_U3_T3#GNS213_U3_T3_h6)

question: During a laryngoscopy, a patient's oxygen level suddenly drops from 98% to 85%. What is your immediate action as the nurse?

options.A: Administer an oral pain medication to relax the vocal cords.
options.B: Document the drop in the chart and wait for the doctor to finish looking.
options.C: Alert the clinician, stop the procedure, and provide supplemental oxygen or bag-valve-mask ventilation.
options.D: Ask the patient to sit up straight and take three deep breaths through their mouth.

explanation: Safety first! A sudden drop in oxygen means you must stop what's happening right away, get help, and give the patient oxygen. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T4#GNS221_U2_T4_h6)

question: Why is it so important to counsel clients about possible changes in their monthly bleeding before putting in an implant?

options.A: Menstrual cycles will completely stop forever within the first week of insertion in all women
options.B: Clients must know that heavy bleeding will require them to take iron pills every single day
options.C: Changes in bleeding indicate that the implant has slipped out of position into the muscle
options.D: Unpredictable bleeding patterns are common and represent the main reason clients request early removal

explanation: No surprises! Giving a heads-up about spotting or lighter periods helps clients stay calm and prevents unnecessary panic or removing the implant too soon. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T014#GNS226_U6_T014_h5)

question: What is the main benefit of using an infusion pump instead of a normal gravity IV line?

options.A: It warms the intravenous fluid before it enters the vein
options.B: It completely removes the need to monitor the IV site
options.C: It delivers fluids at a precise and controlled rate
options.D: It prevents all forms of air embolisms automatically

explanation: Spot on! Infusion pumps give us exact control over how fast fluids run, which is much safer and more reliable than just relying on gravity. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T3#GNS212_U4_T3_h1)

question: Why do modern hospitals emphasize respectful maternity care?

options.A: It guarantees that the baby will be born without any medical issues
options.B: It reduces the cost of building new maternity wards
options.C: It encourages women to choose facility delivery instead of staying home
options.D: It replaces the need for any medications during labor

explanation: Nobody wants to visit a harsh nurse! When women feel welcomed and valued in the clinic, they are happy to come back for safe deliveries. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T001#GNS226_U1_T001_h8)

question: What happens when a patient takes two different medications that both depress the central nervous system?

options.A: Liver enzymes shut down permanently to prevent any chemical processing
options.B: An additive or synergistic sedative effect that can impair breathing
options.C: The two drugs cancel each other out completely with no effect
options.D: The patient experiences a sudden burst of high physical energy

explanation: Combining multiple depressants multiplies their calming effects on the brain and can dangerously slow breathing. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T2#GNS215_U5_T2_h5)

question: In the TNM cancer staging system, what does the letter 'M' stand for?

options.A: Malignancy grade
options.B: Microscopic size
options.C: Metastasis
options.D: Mitosis rate

explanation: You've got this! In TNM staging, 'M' tells us if the cancer has traveled or metastasized to other parts of the body. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T15#GNS324_U4_T15_h5)

question: Why can handing out donated infant formula be dangerous in poorly sanitized displacement camps?

options.A: Unsafe water used to mix formula can cause fatal infant diarrhea.
options.B: Formula milk completely lacks any nutritional value for babies.
options.C: Mothers are physically unable to digest artificial milk ingredients.
options.D: Babies universally reject the taste of artificial milk products.

explanation: Without clean water to mix it and proper ways to sterilize bottles, formula feeding can easily introduce deadly germs to a baby's delicate system. Breastfeeding is safest here! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T21#GNS225_U5_T21_h6)

question: Why is it risky for a nurse to assume direct cause-and-effect from a simple correlational study?

options.A: It violates patient confidentiality laws in the hospital ward
options.B: It can lead to implementing ineffective or incorrect patient care practices
options.C: It means the researcher forgot to calculate the negative numbers
options.D: It guarantees that statistical software will crash during data analysis

explanation: Spot on! Acting on false assumptions can waste precious time and hospital resources on patient care interventions that don't actually work. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T12#GNS224_U1_T12_h7)

question: A patient's surgical wound leaks blood onto the ward floor. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Leave the spill to dry before sweeping it up with a broom
options.B: Mop the area quickly with dry paper towels without wearing gloves
options.C: Put on appropriate gloves and apply a chlorine disinfectant solution over the spill
options.D: Call the administrative office to report a building maintenance issue

explanation: Protecting oneself with barriers and disinfecting the fluid immediately prevents the spread of bloodborne germs. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h6)

question: Which temporary change happens to the maternal brain during pregnancy?

options.A: The permanent destruction of frontal lobe neurons
options.B: An increase in overall brain weight and skull size
options.C: A complete cessation of electrical wave activity
options.D: A temporary reduction in gray matter volume

explanation: Don't worry, moms aren't losing brain power! Gray matter dips slightly as the brain smartly reorganizes its neural networks for parenting. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T6#GNS121_U7_T6_h2)

question: Which of the following is NOT a feature of compact bone when compared to spongy bone?

options.A: It forms the dense and solid outer layer of bones
options.B: It contains an organized system of osteons
options.C: It has a high concentration of red bone marrow inside it
options.D: It provides major structural support for body weight

question: Why do social factors like poverty play such a big role in NCDs?

options.A: They ensure that patients always adhere strictly to their medication regimen
options.B: They directly cause genetic mutations that trigger cancer within weeks
options.C: They limit access to healthy foods, safe exercise spaces, and proper healthcare
options.D: They completely eliminate the risk of developing infectious diseases

explanation: Exactly! When money is tight, it becomes much harder to afford nutritious food, find safe places to exercise, or visit the clinic early for check-ups. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T1#GNS313_U3_T1_h2)

question: Which task is typically part of the management role of a PHC nurse manager?

options.A: Performing major surgical operations independently
options.B: Auditing international pharmaceutical corporations
options.C: Overseeing drug inventories and supervising junior health staff
options.D: Writing national health policy legislation

explanation: PHC nurse managers are responsible for supervising staff and managing daily facility logistics like drug stocks. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T7#GNS124_U2_T7_h7)

question: Why are open-ended questions preferred over closed questions when taking a dietary history?

options.A: They encourage the patient to share more details about their actual habits.
options.B: They allow the nurse to finish the consultation without speaking.
options.C: They take much less time to complete during busy clinic shifts.
options.D: They legally protect the hospital from documentation errors.

explanation: Open-ended questions prevent patients from giving simple yes or no answers, revealing more accurate information about their true diet. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T20#GNS214_U1_T20_h4)

question: What happens to a patient's memory once you start giving them thiamine treatment?

options.A: It cures the underlying liver disease and repairs all brain tissue
options.B: It completely reverses all memory loss within forty-eight hours
options.C: It has no effect whatsoever on the patient's neurological state
options.D: It prevents further worsening, but full recovery of memory is rare

explanation: Thiamine is amazing for stopping the damage from getting worse, but unfortunately, the deep brain changes that already happened are usually permanent. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T8#GNS222_U4_T8_h7)

question: How is oligomenorrhoea different from amenorrhoea?

options.A: Oligomenorrhoea involves infrequent bleeding while amenorrhoea means complete absence of bleeding
options.B: Oligomenorrhoea occurs only in older women while amenorrhoea affects teenagers
options.C: Oligomenorrhoea causes heavy bleeding while amenorrhoea causes painful cramping
options.D: Oligomenorrhoea is a normal variant while amenorrhoea is always pathological

explanation: Nice and clear! Oligomenorrhoea means the periods happen, just less often (infrequent). Amenorrhoea means they have completely stopped (absence). Easy to remember for your exams! [learn more](GNS216_U2_T5#GNS216_U2_T5_h1)

question: What is the main benefit of putting a cold pack on a fresh musculoskeletal injury?

options.A: Reducing acute inflammation and numbing localized discomfort
options.B: Stretching tight tendons before physical exercise begins
options.C: Permanently dissolving hardened scar tissue around the joint
options.D: Increasing local blood flow to speed up muscle contractions

explanation: You got it! Cold constricts blood vessels, which keeps swelling down and numbs the sharp pain right after an activity. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T22#GNS222_U1_T22_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common social barrier to women empowerment in local communities?

options.A: Universal free access to university education for all females
options.B: Religious misinterpretations regarding modern healthcare use
options.C: Patriarchal norms that demand absolute female submission
options.D: Fear of domestic violence or social punishment

explanation: Universal free education is a facilitator of empowerment, not a barrier; the other options represent actual obstacles women face. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T59#GNS214_U1_T59_h4)

question: What do we call a host where a parasite or pathogen grows up and reproduces?

options.A: An organism where the infectious agent reaches maturity and reproduces
options.B: An organism that can catch an infection but never pass it on
options.C: An environmental source where bacteria live without growing
options.D: An insect that only carries a virus on its outer legs

question: What is the biggest danger that causes high complications in unsafe abortions?

options.A: Early detection of pregnancy in a regulated hospital setting
options.B: The use of untrained providers and unsterile conditions
options.C: Regular monitoring by professional obstetric nurses
options.D: The prescription of standard medical abortion pills by doctors

question: Why are the three semicircular canals placed at right angles to each other?

options.A: To make room for the auditory nerve inside the skull
options.B: To detect rotational movement in all three spatial dimensions
options.C: To allow equal pressure distribution of perilymph fluid
options.D: To prevent the endolymph from flowing too quickly

explanation: This clever layout lets your brain pick up movement in every direction: up and down, side to side, and tilting! [learn more](GNS211_U4_T8#GNS211_U4_T8_h2)

question: A nurse is arguing loudly with a doctor at the nursing station. What type of conflict is this?

options.A: Intragroup conflict
options.B: Intrapersonal conflict
options.C: Interpersonal conflict
options.D: Organizational conflict

explanation: Anytime two or more distinct people are clashing or disagreeing, that's an interpersonal conflict. You'll see this often on the wards, and it's a great chance to practice good communication! [learn more](GST321_U5_T1#GST321_U5_T1_h2)

question: What is the very first step a nurse should take when entering a new community for health mobilisation?

options.A: Administering vaccines without telling anyone first
options.B: Visiting local leaders to gain entry and approval
options.C: Building a clinic fence using community donations
options.D: Conducting a written examination for all adults

question: Why must you check when a patient had their last tetanus shot before stitching up a wound?

options.A: To determine if the patient needs protection against tetanus spores in dirty wounds
options.B: To check how fast the patient's blood will normally clot
options.C: To decide what type of local anesthetic to inject
options.D: To calculate the exact day the sutures should be removed

explanation: Cuts can easily trap dirt and tetanus bacteria. Checking their history helps us know if they need a booster shot to stay safe. Simple and lifesaving! [learn more](GNS311_U4_T2#GNS311_U4_T2_h1)

question: What is an important nursing duty when a pregnant patient is given an antiemetic drug?

options.A: Encourage the patient to stop taking all oral fluids
options.B: Advise the patient to double the dose if nausea returns
options.C: Check fetal heart tones every fifteen minutes around the clock
options.D: Monitor the patient for common side effects like drowsiness

explanation: Many antiemetics make patients sleepy. Keeping an eye on safety and advising them about drowsiness is a key nursing role. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T011#GNS226_U2_T011_h5)

question: Roughly how many extra calories per day does producing breast milk require on average?

options.A: 100 calories
options.B: 1200 calories
options.C: 50 calories
options.D: 500 calories

explanation: Milk production is metabolically demanding, requiring about 500 extra calories daily for an exclusively breastfeeding mother. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T013#GNS227_U2_T013_h2)

question: Why does a nurse use the back of the hand when checking skin temperature over a swollen joint?

options.A: It is required by standard infection control guidelines for wound care
options.B: The skin on the dorsal hand is thinner and more sensitive to temperature changes
options.C: It prevents the patient from feeling intimidated by a direct palm touch
options.D: The palm is too warm to detect minor differences in body heat

explanation: The thin skin on the back of the hand is much better at detecting subtle variations in local skin warmth. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T3#GNS222_U1_T3_h4)

question: Which vaccine is routinely given to newborns to protect against severe forms of childhood TB?

options.A: OPV vaccine
options.B: BCG vaccine
options.C: MMR vaccine
options.D: Tetanus toxoid

explanation: The BCG vaccine is given early in life to give babies strong backup against the most dangerous, widespread forms of childhood TB. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T5#GNS214_U1_T5_h7)

question: Why does Staphylococcus food poisoning cause sudden vomiting very soon after eating?

options.A: It blocks normal movement in the large intestine
options.B: It destroys the stomach lining with acid
options.C: It produces toxins in the food before you even eat it
options.D: It multiplies inside the bloodstream instantly

explanation: Think of Staph as leaving nasty toxins behind in food left out too long. Once you eat it, those pre-made toxins trigger rapid vomiting. Makes total sense, right? [learn more](GNS227_U3_T010#GNS227_U3_T010_h2)

question: What is the main difference between recruitment and selection?

options.A: Recruitment finds candidates, while selection chooses the best fit
options.B: Recruitment checks licenses, while selection checks exam scores
options.C: Selection is done by human resources, and recruitment is done by doctors
options.D: There is no difference between the two terms

explanation: Recruitment brings people in to apply, and selection is the screening process used to pick the right hire. [learn more](GST321_U1_T11#GST321_U1_T11_h3)

question: What must a nurse check before giving fluids to someone who just had surgery?

options.A: Testing the patient's long-term memory function
options.B: Checking for the presence of bowel sounds
options.C: Assessing the patient's skin color on the lower extremities
options.D: Measuring the patient's exact daily walking distance

explanation: Listening for bowel sounds tells you if the gut has woken up from anesthesia and is ready to process anything. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T001#GNS227_U6_T001_h5)

question: What is the main goal of the family planning referral method in community nursing?

options.A: To connect clients to specialized or unavailable reproductive health services
options.B: To permanently discharge clients from primary health care facilities
options.C: To reduce the overall number of children born in a specific community
options.D: To decrease the administrative workload of community health nurses

explanation: Think of a referral as a helpful bridge! When a client needs care or family planning methods that your local clinic cannot provide, you connect them to a place that can. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T6#GNS225_U3_T6_h1)

question: If you are calculating the incidence of a uterine infection, who belongs at the bottom (the denominator)?

options.A: Every single person living in the entire country
options.B: All children under the age of five years old
options.C: Only individuals with a uterus who are at risk
options.D: Only patients who already have the infection

explanation: Well done! The denominator should only include the people who are actually at risk of catching that specific condition. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T11#GNS313_U1_T11_h2)

question: What is anticipatory grief?

options.A: Anger directed at doctors after a misdiagnosis
options.B: Depression caused by a sudden physical injury
options.C: Grief experienced before the actual death occurs
options.D: Relief felt when a patient finally passes away

explanation: Anticipatory grief is the mourning process that happens prior to an expected death as losses accumulate. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T16#GNS321_U4_T16_h6)

question: Which two common sexually transmitted bacteria are most often linked to pelvic inflammatory disease?

options.A: Candida albicans and Trichomonas vaginalis
options.B: Human papillomavirus and Herpes simplex
options.C: Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus
options.D: Chlamydia trachomatis and Neisseria gonorrhoeae

question: What is the most crucial thing to teach a patient before they leave the hospital after recovering from a tummy bug?

options.B: Warning signs and red flags that mean they need to return to the clinic
options.C: To avoid all physical movement for six full months
options.D: Where to buy expensive herbal gut supplements

explanation: Patients must know what danger signs to watch for at home so they can get help early before a small issue blows up into an emergency. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T13#GNS213_U3_T13_h7)

question: How does the daily work of a PHC nurse differ mainly from a nurse in a high-tech hospital ICU?

options.A: The hospital nurse spends most of their time farming and digging boreholes
options.B: The PHC nurse focuses heavily on community outreach, health promotion, and preventive education
options.C: The PHC nurse is forbidden from touching patients or administering medications
options.D: The PHC nurse only provides end-of-life care and palliative treatments

explanation: Well done! While hospital nurses focus heavily on treating acute illness, PHC nurses focus on keeping the wider community well through prevention and health education. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T3#GNS124_U1_T3_h6)

question: How does a cold compress help reduce pain?

options.A: By increasing the local metabolic rate of damaged cells
options.B: By slowing down nerve conduction velocity to numb the site
options.C: By permanently destroying local sensory pain receptors
options.D: By flushing out inflammatory toxins through massive vasodilation

question: Which specialized bone cell is responsible for breaking down or resorbing bone tissue?

options.A: Osteocyte
options.B: Osteoclast
options.C: Osteoblast
options.D: Chondrocyte

question: You want to find out what a patient ate over the past 24 hours. Which assessment tool should you use?

options.A: A physical skin examination
options.B: An anthropometric weighing
options.C: A 24-hour food recall
options.D: A biochemical blood draw

question: A home health nurse visits a patient with chronic heart failure. Which action best supports long-term disease management?

options.A: Advising the patient to eat as much salted food as they want
options.B: Telling the patient to stop taking all prescribed daily water pills
options.C: Teaching the patient how to weigh themselves daily and track swelling
options.D: Discharging the patient from care because the disease is ongoing

explanation: Daily weight tracking helps catch fluid retention early before it turns into a dangerous heart failure flare-up. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T8#GNS324_U1_T8_h2)

question: What is the main strategy used to treat most cases of acute poisoning in the hospital?

options.A: High-dose antibiotic therapy
options.B: Complete sensory deprivation
options.C: Immediate surgical removal of the stomach
options.D: Supportive care and managing symptoms

explanation: Don't stress trying to memorize an antidote for everything—most poisons don't have one! The core treatment is simply keeping vital organs working smoothly until the body clears the poison on its own. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T6#GNS215_U5_T6_h6)

question: When is the second medication safety check typically performed?

options.A: While preparing or pouring the medication
options.B: When removing the drug from the storage shelf
options.C: During the morning nursing handover meeting
options.D: After the patient has swallowed the pill

question: A diabetic patient insists on participating in a religious fast that could affect their blood sugar. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Discharge the patient immediately for being uncooperative
options.B: Tell the patient that religion has no place in modern healthcare
options.C: Collaborate with the patient to find safe ways to manage blood sugar during the fast
options.D: Force the patient to eat hospital meals against their religious beliefs

explanation: Respecting patient autonomy and beliefs while finding safe health compromises is the core of ethical nursing care. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T001#GNS227_U7_T001_h6)

question: A cancer patient is exercising. Which sign means you should stop the activity right away?

options.A: A slight increase in heart rate during active movement

options.C: Sudden chest pain, severe shortness of breath, and dizziness
options.D: Desire to rest after completing a supervised stretching routine

explanation: Always watch out for red flags! Chest pain, dizziness, and trouble breathing mean the heart or lungs are struggling during exercise. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T11#GNS321_U1_T11_h6)

question: Which condition is a primary indication for a low salt diet in hospital wards?

options.B: Acute bone fractures
options.C: Type 1 diabetes mellitus
options.D: Iron deficiency anemia

question: Which term describes a histogram where the left and right sides mirror each other around a center peak?

question: Why do many rural families traditionally view having many children as a great benefit?

options.B: Children provide farm labor and security in old age
options.C: Larger households receive free agricultural land allotments
options.D: School fees are fully subsidized for families with five children

question: How is a purpose statement different from a problem statement?

options.A: The problem statement contains all the final conclusions
options.B: The problem statement is written after data is collected
options.C: The purpose statement only lists financial costs
options.D: The purpose statement declares the direct aim or goal of the study

question: When listening to the chest of a patient with lung consolidation, what sound do you usually hear?

options.B: A friction rub in the neck
options.C: Stridor
options.D: Borborygmi

question: What is the main way drugs are grouped by their origin?

options.C: The exact cost of manufacturing the drug
options.D: Their original source and how they are made

question: How can long-term social isolation negatively affect an older adult?

options.A: It stops them from developing age-related illnesses
options.B: It permanently improves their ability to stay calm
options.C: It weakens immune function and worsens mental health
options.D: It increases their daily physical endurance levels

question: Why do dry-heat cooking methods create brown crusts and rich flavors on food?

options.A: They use high temperatures that trigger the Maillard reaction on the food surface.
options.B: They rely on water molecules to break down complex sugars into simple starches.
options.C: They add liquid fats that caramelize quickly when exposed to steam.

explanation: When high dry heat hits proteins and sugars on the surface, it causes the famous Maillard reaction—giving us that wonderful roasted aroma and golden crust. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T008#GNS227_U3_T008_h4)

question: What does the acronym NEAT stand for in energy expenditure?

options.A: Non-exercise activity thermogenesis
options.B: Nutritional energy and tissue
options.C: Net enteral absorption time
options.D: Normal electrolyte and acid test

explanation: NEAT stands for non-exercise activity thermogenesis, covering all daily movements outside of formal workouts. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T008#GNS227_U4_T008_h4)

question: A hospital notices multiple incident reports about look-alike drug vials. What is the best quality improvement action?

options.A: Stop ordering that medication entirely without finding an alternative

options.C: Fire the nurses who reported the confusing packaging

question: What is the primary purpose of mechanical digestion?

options.A: To change proteins directly into amino acids
options.B: To neutralize stomach acid before food enters the bowel
options.C: To transport nutrients through the intestinal wall
options.D: To increase the surface area of food for enzymes

question: What is a major lung complication that often happens to patients who are unconscious and immobile for a long time?

options.A: Hypostatic pneumonia
options.B: Pulmonary hypertension

options.D: Spontaneous pneumothorax

question: What is the main reason teenagers often avoid seeking healthcare for sensitive personal issues?

options.A: Preference for traditional herbal remedies only

options.D: The high cost of prescription eyeglasses

question: What is the primary focus of assertive communication?

options.A: Placing patient needs above all laws
options.B: Winning every professional argument
options.C: Expressing needs while respecting others
options.D: Avoiding all forms of workplace conflict

explanation: Assertiveness balances your own rights and needs with respect for the rights and needs of the people around you. [learn more](GST321_U7_T5#GST321_U7_T5_h1)

question: In which of these situations is giving a strong purgative UNSAFE?

options.A: When a patient has acute abdominal pain of unknown origin
options.B: When a patient needs to avoid straining after childbirth
options.C: When managing mild constipation caused by dietary changes
options.D: When preparing an adult patient for a scheduled colonoscopy

question: What is the main mindset shift behind trauma-informed care?

options.A: Asking what happened to the patient instead of what is wrong with them
options.B: Minimizing emotional expressions to maintain clinical efficiency
options.C: Determining the legal guilt of the alleged perpetrator immediately
options.D: Focusing exclusively on surgical repair of physical wounds

explanation: Instead of judging a patient's behavior, trauma-informed care reminds us to ask, 'What happened to you?' It's all about empathy. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T13#GNS312_U4_T13_h5)

question: What happens at the cellular level right when a seizure starts?

options.A: Excessive neuronal excitation combined with a failure of inhibition
options.B: Massive overproduction of cerebrospinal fluid in the ventricles
options.C: Rapid destruction of myelin sheaths along peripheral nerves
options.D: Complete depletion of glucose stores within glial cells

explanation: Seizures happen when brain signals become too excited and the brain's natural 'brakes' (inhibition) fail to slow them down. You are building strong clinical instincts! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T9#GNS222_U4_T9_h2)

question: What does equity in a healthcare budget mean?

options.A: Distributing health services fairly so vulnerable populations receive care
options.B: Giving every single department the exact same amount of cash
options.C: Allowing only wealthy patients to access specialized treatments
options.D: Ensuring the hospital makes a profit on every patient admitted

explanation: Budgetary equity focuses on fair distribution so that those in need, including vulnerable groups, can access care. [learn more](GST322_U2_T4#GST322_U2_T4_h2)

question: A patient near a fast-flowing river has firm, painless lumps over their hip bones and very itchy skin. What is the most likely condition?

options.C: Onchocerciasis

question: What does finding chorioamnionitis on a delivered placenta tell you?

options.D: A previous cesarean section scar

question: What three areas does the Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) assess?

options.A: Blood pressure, heart rate, and temperature
options.B: Swallowing reflex, pupil size, and skin color
options.C: Eye opening, verbal response, and motor response
options.D: Pain tolerance, mood, and cognitive memory

explanation: The GCS is a quick, reliable way to check a patient's level of consciousness by testing these three clear reactions. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T23#GNS222_U3_T23_h7)

question: What is the primary goal of leadership in community health practice?

options.A: Empowering communities to manage their own health
options.B: Reducing the operational costs of local clinics
options.C: Enforcing strict compliance with national hospital policies
options.D: Directing all medical treatment decisions without input

explanation: Community leadership focuses on working alongside the population so they can eventually direct and sustain their own health improvements. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T2#GNS124_U2_T2_h1)

question: What is the main feature of a cross-sectional study?

options.A: The researcher changes the treatment given to patients

options.C: Data is gathered only from patients who have recovered
options.D: Patients are followed up over several years

question: What usually happens to red bone marrow in long bones as a person grows older?

options.A: It transforms into active cartilage tissue.
options.B: It turns into yellow bone marrow for fat storage.
options.C: It dissolves completely leaving empty hollow spaces.
options.D: It hardens directly into compact cortical bone.

explanation: As we age, our bodies don't need quite as much active red marrow making blood cells all the time. Much of it converts into yellow marrow, which mainly stores fat (though it can switch back to red if the body urgently needs it!). [learn more](GNS121_U3_T3#GNS121_U3_T3_h4)

question: Why is teaching community members about injection safety so important in Nigeria?

options.A: To cut down the cost of running clinics
options.B: To replace nursing school training
options.C: To help patients understand they don't always need an injection
options.D: To teach patients to give themselves IV drugs at home

explanation: Many people believe injections work faster than tablets, leading to a huge demand for unnecessary shots. Educating the public keeps everyone safer. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T1#GNS122_U4_T1_h6)

question: A pregnant patient refuses to eat meat because she heard it causes birth defects. How should you handle this as her nurse?

options.A: Force her to eat the meat immediately during the clinic visit
options.B: Scold the patient for believing foolish stories
options.C: Recognize this as a cultural myth and gently offer safe protein alternatives
options.D: Ignore her diet since beliefs have no impact on pregnancy

explanation: Always respect your patient's background! Providing gentle, accurate education and helping them find alternative protein sources builds great trust. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T017#GNS227_U2_T017_h3)

question: Which Nigerian agency coordinates national policies and responses related to HIV?

question: Why is using a shared conceptual framework useful for spreading evidence-based practice?

options.A: It stops nurses from asking questions about new procedures

options.C: It removes the need for patient consent during studies
options.D: It makes clinical guidelines completely optional for staff

explanation: When all nurses speak the same clinical language, it is much easier to share what works and improve patient care together. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T11#GNS217_U3_T11_h6)

question: Which observation should you report to the physical therapist before their next session?

question: In statistics, what is another helpful name for an ogive graph?

question: What is the best nursing action right after a patient passes away?

options.A: Removing all personal belongings of the deceased immediately

question: A young, unmarried woman leaves a clinic without birth control because the nurse scolds her. What is this barrier called?

options.A: Healthcare provider bias

options.C: Geographic isolation
options.D: Commodity stock-out

question: How does a severe climate disaster like a drought hurt a farming community's nutrition?

options.C: By encouraging families to plant diverse crops for the next season

question: Why do toxins breathed into the lungs (inhalation) affect the body so quickly?

question: What happens in the colon when someone doesn't drink enough water?

question: What kind of information do you mainly gather when taking a patient's health history?

question: Why do perpetrators usually carry out breast ironing?

question: What does 'generalizability' mean in a nursing research study?

question: Which part of the stethoscope is best suited for hearing low-pitched murmurs like S3 or S4?

question: A patient takes a normal dose of a drug and gets unexpected liver failure that isn't an allergy. How should you classify this as a nurse?

question: A nurse places a naked newborn onto a cold metal scale, making the baby lose body heat. What is this specific type of heat loss called?

question: At what time of day is a blood test most accurate for checking testosterone levels?

question: Why must a woman with an intact uterus take progesterone along with estrogen replacement therapy?

question: Why are asymptomatic carriers so tricky to deal with during disease outbreaks?

question: A patient comes in with swollen lower legs, brownish skin around the ankles, and a dull ache that gets worse when standing. What condition is most likely?

question: What is the best immediate step for a clinic facing a sudden stockout of syringes?

question: Which of these is a clear example of emotional abuse?

question: A Nigerian nurse is talking with a mother during a routine immunization visit. What is a great way to use this time for nutrition?

question: If a family suddenly loses income due to a job loss, what dietary change is most likely to happen first?

question: Where should a nurse NOT use a local anesthetic mixed with adrenaline?

question: What happens in the body when alpha cells release glucagon into the bloodstream?

question: What is the main danger of a cytokine storm in severe COVID-19 patients?

question: Which lab results are most important for a nurse to check before starting a patient on anti-bleeding therapy?

question: When someone breathes in gases or vapors, why do they get absorbed into the body so quickly?

question: A clinic notices a sudden drop in teenagers coming in for counseling. What is the best next step?

question: How do the ureters move urine down from the kidneys into the bladder?

question: What important advice should a nurse give a patient using the misoprostol-only method?

question: Why shouldn't a researcher just repeat the results in the discussion section?

question: What is the main focus of 'andragogy'?

question: What is the main purpose of 'socialization' within any community?

question: A patient with a suspected deep bone infection of the tibia needs detailed bone imaging. Why is a CT scan chosen over a basic x-ray?

question: Why are newborn babies and burn patients at higher risk of chemical absorption from skin antiseptics?

question: At what point does the first stage of labour officially end?

question: Why must dangerous infections like cholera or yellow fever be classified as notifiable diseases?

question: What is the main purpose of giving a blood transfusion to a patient with acute haemorrhage?

options.A: To prevent the kidneys from producing any urine
options.B: To speed up the digestion of food in the stomach
options.C: To replace lost red blood cells and restore oxygen delivery
options.D: To lower the patient's elevated body temperature

explanation: Transfusions supply the red blood cells needed to carry oxygen to tissues when the patient's own blood volume is dangerously depleted. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T2#GNS112_U7_T2_h6)

question: A client says they wore a condom inside out, flipped it, and kept going. What is your best nursing advice?

options.A: Suggest washing the condom with soap and reusing it
options.B: Recommend taking emergency contraception immediately
options.C: Tell them the method is completely safe
options.D: Advise discarding it because pre-seminal fluid may be on the outside

explanation: Good clinical thinking! Flipping it exposes the inside part—which might already have pre-ejaculatory fluid—to the partner, raising infection and pregnancy risks. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T018#GNS226_U6_T018_h5)

question: Which cranial nerves have their roots located right inside the brain stem?

options.A: Cranial nerves III through XII
options.B: Only the spinal accessory nerve
options.C: All twelve pairs of cranial nerves
options.D: Cranial nerves I and II only

explanation: Ten out of the twelve pairs of cranial nerves (from number three to twelve) actually originate right inside the brain stem. Neat, right? [learn more](GNS211_U3_T18#GNS211_U3_T18_h2)

question: A nurse accidentally pricks a finger with a used needle of unknown status. What is the very first thing to do?

options.A: Fill out an incident report form for the hospital human resources
options.B: Begin taking a 28-day course of antibiotics immediately
options.C: Call the patient back to the clinic for a rapid blood test
options.D: Wash the puncture wound thoroughly with soap and clean water

explanation: Correct! Immediate first aid means rushing to wash the site with soap and water to rinse away germs. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T9#GNS216_U6_T9_h5)

question: Why is it so important to help a mother keep her bladder empty during prolonged labour?

options.A: It lowers the mother's blood pressure instantly
options.B: It prevents the kidneys from producing urine altogether
options.C: It stops the uterus from contracting spontaneously
options.D: A full bladder can obstruct fetal descent and slow labour

explanation: Think of the pelvic space as crowded! A full bladder gets in the way, making it harder for the baby's head to move down naturally. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T010#GNS226_U4_T010_h5)

question: Which of the following is considered a classic sign of maternal depletion that a nurse should watch out for?

options.A: Chronic fatigue and hair loss
options.B: Rapid thickening of tooth enamel
options.C: Decreased need for hours of sleep
options.D: Sudden increase in physical stamina

explanation: When a mother's nutritional stores run low to support milk production, she may experience exhaustion, hair thinning, and fatigue. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T009#GNS227_U2_T009_h8)

question: Which common blood test checks for both anemia and signs of infection?

options.A: Blood Glucose Test
options.B: Complete Blood Count
options.C: Urinalysis
options.D: Malaria Parasite Test

explanation: A Complete Blood Count (CBC) looks at your red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets. It is super helpful for spotting anemia and infections! Keep it up. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T4#GNS124_U6_T4_h3)

question: What is the most frequent cause of heavy bleeding after delivery (postpartum hemorrhage) in grand multiparous women?

options.A: Uterine atony
options.B: Uterine inversion
options.C: Retained placental fragments
options.D: Cervical laceration

explanation: Uterine atony happens when the womb muscles fail to clamp down tightly after the baby is born, leaving blood vessels wide open to bleed. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T008#GNS226_U4_T008_h5)

question: How does putting a heating pad on the lower belly help with post-abortion cramps?

options.A: It stops all vaginal bleeding instantly
options.B: It numbs the skin nerves permanently
options.C: It relaxes the uterine and pelvic muscles
options.D: It lowers the body temperature safely

explanation: Warmth boosts blood flow and helps tense muscles unwind, taking the sharp edge off those cramps. Simple and effective nursing comfort care! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T014#GNS226_U5_T014_h4)

question: What minimum percentage of adherence is needed for antiretroviral therapy to work successfully?
explanation: You nailed it! Patients need to take at least 95% of their doses on time to keep the virus suppressed and stop resistance. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T13#GNS215_U6_T13_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT allowed when conducting ethical nursing research?

options.A: Forcing patients to participate to get a large sample size
options.B: Protecting the privacy and confidentiality of patients
options.C: Ensuring participants are protected from physical harm
options.D: Obtaining informed consent from every participant

explanation: Participation in research must always be totally voluntary. Patients should never feel pressured or forced to join! [learn more](GNS217_U3_T4#GNS217_U3_T4_h4)

question: Why do community health clinics use standardized monthly reporting templates?

options.A: They replace the need for individual patient client cards
options.B: They allow local health posts to aggregate and transmit data upward to health authorities
options.C: They serve as personal journals for nurses to write daily reflections
options.D: They act as legal contracts between patients and the hospital

explanation: Spot on! Standardized templates make sure data flows smoothly and clearly from local grassroots clinics all the way up to national health planners. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T13#GNS225_U2_T13_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT a typical challenge when patients try to change their diet?

options.A: Unsupportive family members in the home
options.B: Financial constraints and high food costs
options.C: Excessive availability of free clinical dietitians
options.D: Lack of cooking skills or kitchen facilities

explanation: Correct! Having access to helpful dietitians is a blessing, not a barrier. The real struggles are usually money, time, and kitchen setups. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T005#GNS227_U7_T005_h6)

question: In public health and nursing, what do the letters IEC stand for?

options.A: Investigation, Empowerment, and Cure
options.B: Immunization, Environment, and Control
options.C: Illness, Evaluation, and Care
options.D: Information, Education, and Communication

explanation: IEC stands for Information, Education, and Communication. You'll use these core tools every day in community health to spread awareness and help people stay healthy! [learn more](GNS124_U5_T7#GNS124_U5_T7_h1)
